summary: This article explains how islands form through volcanoes, coral, and separation from continents, with examples from around the world, and how living on an island differs from living on the mainland.
introduce: Write “Alike” and “Different” at the top of a T-chart on the board and ask students to compare two school subjects in one minute. Explain that “Islands: Land in the Middle of Water” asks them to make the same kind of comparison.

keyTerms.def: a large group of islands scattered close together in the sea
cut off or separated from other things or places
the slow wearing away of rock or soil by wind, water, or waves

challengeTerms.def: found naturally in only one place and nowhere else
relating to a large landmass, or a continent, rather than an island
relating to the huge moving plates that make up the Earth's crust

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that living on an island would be very different from living on the mainland? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how islands form in different ways, and explain one way that life on an island differs from life on the mainland.
struggling: Pre-teach archipelago, isolated, and erosion with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use endemic, continental, and tectonic in a short paragraph that compares two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
